text:
Nadia: FYI — Acme Payments reporting a spike of 429s in prod starting ~2026-02-25 16:10 UTC. They say project dashboard shows ~85% of project quota, API key reports no obvious errors. They sent a sample request and claim their provider runs through a proxy. Can someone triage? :eyes:

Tom: Do we have a request_id or sample raw request? need headers (Authorization + any X-Forwarded-For) and a few timestamps so I can match in logs.

Nadia: Paste from customer (redacted):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ak-prod-123" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -H "X-Forwarded-For: 44.55.66.77" 
  -d '{"model":"gpt-xx","input":"..."}'
```
They say thousands of clients are behind that single egress IP.

rate-limiter-bot: limit-check: REJECTED -> scope=ip:44.55.66.77 limit=100r/s window=1s project=acme-prod api_key=ak-prod-123 outcome=throttled rule_id=ip_global_100s

Lee: Ah — looks like the ip_global_100s rule fired. Quick explanation: we have layered quotas: api-key scoped and project-scoped quotas are evaluated, but we also apply a global per-IP rate limiter as an extra guard for noisy NATs and misbehaving proxies. That per-IP guard can be lower than the project quota and will cause 429s even when project usage is fine.

Ava: Another edge case to watch: if a request arrives missing/invalid Authorization (or we fail to map the key to a project for a short period) we fall back to IP attribution for throttling decisions. If the proxy sometimes strips headers or rewrites auth, those intermittent failures can flip requests into the IP-path.

Tom: Two quick repro suggestions for SRE/support to confirm:
1) From a machine that will present as 44.55.66.77 (or via the proxy), run a burst to match the check:
```bash
# synthetic burst to trigger ip global limiter
hey -n 1000 -c 200 -m POST -H "Authorization: Bearer ak-prod-123" -H "X-Forwarded-For: 44.55.66.77" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
2) Repeat but omit Authorization header to see whether requests are falling back to ip-only buckets.

Lee: Also use this log query to cross-check both attribution paths (API key vs IP):
```sql
SELECT timestamp, request_id, auth_key, client_ip, rule_triggered
FROM request_rate_logs
WHERE client_ip = '44.55.66.77'
AND timestamp >= '2026-02-25T16:00:00Z'
ORDER BY timestamp DESC
LIMIT 200;
```
(returns both auth_key values and rule_triggered field so you can see if some hits had auth_key=NULL)

Nadia: Customer tried rotating the key to a new one and still saw intermittent 429s. They insisted the Authorization header is present from their side. They suspect their proxy sometimes terminates TLS and re-makes requests — might strip headers.

Ava: If proxy terminates TLS and re-issues requests, ensure it forwards Authorization and preserves the original client IP in X-Forwarded-For. If not, you get collapsing of many tenants onto one IP and the IP limiter will bite. Options: ask them to forward original IPs, use mutual TLS between proxy and our edge, or give them a dedicated egress IP pool (if they control infra).

Tom: For an immediate mitigation we can: (a) temporarily raise the ip_global_100s bucket for that specific IP, (b) create a per-project override that exempts requests authenticated with ak-prod-123 from that specific ip rule, or (c) advise customer to move traffic to a different egress IP. Which do we want?

Lee: I can do (a) for a short window while we collect traces. If we do (b) we need to add a rule that matches project + ip -> higher threshold; that's safe but requires change control. Note: raising ip_global for one IP is pretty low risk.

OpsBot: change-request: bump ip_global_100s limit for 44.55.66.77 to 400r/s for 60 minutes. ticket=SN-4629 action=applied by=OpsBot

Nadia: Thanks — customer will test in 10 minutes and report back. I'll ask them to capture a single request_id when they see a 429.

Tom: Follow-up checklist for post-mitigation: 1) confirm no auth_key=NULL hits for that IP in logs; 2) audit proxy config for header passthrough; 3) recommend longer-term: per-project reserved capacity or Dedicated if steady high throughput.

Ava: Small gotcha we found previously: some older SDK versions drop Authorization if they see an unknown proxy chain header. If customer uses SDK, ask them to upgrade to latest.

Nadia: Customer confirms reduced 429s after the bump. They're going to rotate proxy config and report. I'll file a short RCA if we see recurrence. Thanks everyone :heart:
